card.name: Arrest, exile and death-date contexts
card.fires_on: Words in biographical or historical text where a person is caught, arrested, exiled or forced to flee, and the spot where a death date is given. It fires on the linking word or name part just before the outcome is stated.

modes.label: Capture or exile
modes.description: Linking words or name endings right after someone is caught, arrested, sent into exile or forced to flee.
modes.example: In the meantime, in 335 the emperor commanded Athanasius to go<< into>> exile at Trier in Germany.

modes.label: Death dates in biographies
modes.description: The space or the word died just before the day or year in a birth-and-death entry.

card.writes: It promotes words for arrest, escape, fugitive and exile, mostly Chinese terms, so it pushes toward flight-or-capture vocabulary.
card.plain: It lights up in history and biography text when someone is arrested, exiled or flees, and also in life-date entries.
